To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

verbal working memory for visual stimuli is associated with a spatially stable occipito-frontoparietal desynchrony, which increases in amplitude over time, and that no significant changes in event-related fields (i.e., the sum of the oscillatory activity) were observed during information maintenance.

1) the verbal working memory is associated with oscillations in the alpha and beta bands; 2) the oscillatory activity is distributed in time and in space and 3) it is not possible to detect changes in event-related fields in areas where significant oscillatory changes are noted.

verbal working memory is associated with oscillatory activity in the occipital and left frontoparietal areas, and the activity is consistent with the hypothesis of oscillatory interplay of the brain areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the neural generators of the brain rhythms associated with verbal working-memory processes.
the temporal and spatial dimensions of neural oscillations associated with verbal working-memory processes.
the analysis of oscillations associated with verbal working memories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

verbal working memory is associated with a dynamic interplay between occipital and left frontotemporal areas, which is characterized by a spatially stable desynchronization in the theta band during information encoding, a spatially stable synchronization in the alpha band during information maintenance, and an increasing left frontotemporo-occipital desynchronization in the alpha band over time.
the brain is not only an electrical organ, but also a dynamic one.
oscillations are not the only way to understand brain function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural oscillatory activity in different frequency bands is associated with different cognitive operations.
the brain uses different frequency bands to perform different cognitive functions and that these frequency bands can be localized in space.

verbal working memory is a dynamic process that involves the interplay of different areas of the brain, which is associated with oscillatory activity that can be observed in the time, spatial, and frequency domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oscillatory activity can be used to track the time course of cognitive processes, even when these processes do not produce a detectable ERF.
the tridimensional analysis is a useful method for detecting the neural generators underlying verbal working memory.
the temporal, spatial and frequency dimensions of the brain's activity should be considered in order to better understand the brain mechanisms of cognitive operations.
